key_insight: Thermally sprayed oxide coatings on 304 stainless steel can act as stable barrier layers against molten Al-Si and Al-Cu-Si phase change materials without obvious degradation under long exposure or cycling.
engineering_relevance: These coatings improve container compatibility for high-temperature latent heat thermal energy storage, enabling safer and more durable stainless-steel hardware for aluminium-based mPCM systems.
method: APS and HVSFS oxide coatings were deposited directly on 304 stainless steel.
Coatings studied: Al2O3, ZrO2, and Al2O3/ZrO2 (60/40 wt. %).
Performance was checked by static compatibility, thermal cycling, and thermal contact resistance tests.
evidence_signal: After two weeks of static exposure and about 300 thermal cycles, the study reports no reaction layers, no coating dissolution, no detectable interdiffusion, and liquid thermal contact resistances of 0.31×10^-3 and 0.39×10^-3 m² K W^-1 for smooth and rough interfaces.
watch_item: Results are promising but are based on limited laboratory exposure durations and specific coating/process conditions, so long-term industrial durability and scale-up still need confirmation.
paper_title: Thermal Sprayed Oxide Coatings for Stainless Steel Containers Used with Molten Al–Si and Al–Cu–Si Phase Change Materials: Compatibility and Thermal Cycling Stability
